central_topic: Conditional task-support investment needed for a fixed target model to become strictly first on public multi-task score matrices under mean, median, and trimmed-mean aggregation, with bounded score uplifts and explicit attainment certificates.
core_methods: Fixed-rival score-space intervention: selected coordinates change from x_j to x_j + alpha*(1-x_j), with alpha in {0.25, 0.5, 1}; investment is selected-task cardinality or its panel-normalized fraction, not measured training cost
Equal-weight arithmetic mean, conventional median averaging the two middle values for even panels, and symmetric trimmed mean dropping floor(0.2*m) scores from each end
Exact sorted-headroom support selection for the mean and exhaustive support enumeration for panels of at most six tasks
Deterministic marginal-aggregate greedy support selection for larger median and trimmed-mean panels, verified against fixed rivals with strict-first tolerance 1e-10
Conservative lower bounds and feasible support witnesses distinguishing optimal, bounded/unresolved, and infeasible decisions
comparators: Robust statistics and finite-sample sensitivity of medians and trimmed means; estimator robustness is not automatically leaderboard manipulation resistance
Social-choice approaches to multi-task agent evaluation; ordinal aggregation is related work, not an implemented comparator
Strategic post-training incentives; contrast multi-developer strategic models with this run's single-target, fixed-rival counterfactual
Task-selection sensitivity and the benchmark lottery
Evaluation-data contamination as motivation and a limitation of interpreting assumed score uplifts causally
Executed no-intervention, random-order, and marginal-greedy support baselines; no separate generic optimization literature search is needed for these elementary controls
benchmarks: HELM MMLU release v1.13.0: 57 subject-score coordinates

result_driven_themes: Conditional attainability under response ceilings: final evaluation reports both attainment shortfalls and attained targets; alpha is an assumed score-response parameter, not a measured training response
Exact small-panel certification versus nonzero aggregate certificate gaps on the evaluated workload; a feasible greedy witness need not establish minimum support
Task granularity and panel selection delimit interpretation across subject-level MMLU, six-task contents scores, and separate BBH sensitivity panels; this is not architecture transfer
No qualifying search winner was found and the baseline was selected; proposed rank-window and coupled-clipped variants do not support claims of methodological improvement
No evidence establishes a universal robustness ordering among the three aggregation rules or an empirical cost of actual contamination
